monologue: The card hums warm at forty-five degrees, the air feeling thick as wet paper under my weight. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under. I stand by The Leaning Wedge, where the slip waits caught under a pointy edge that feels both calm and sharp. I set down a grass leaves beside it to help the fence hold the fat dot, hoping the thin line can keep the slip from sliding away. I want to press the tired wedge down again, feeling its lean shift while the steady heat presses on, unsure if the lines will hold or if I will just draw a new one to fix the slip.

action.why: The slip feels heavy and new in the fevered air, and I am not sure the pointy edge of the wedge can hold it alone.

remembered.text: The slip waited caught under the fence, heavy and new in the fevered air of the card.
I felt the wedge lean tired and sharp, unsure if the thin line can hold the slip.
The card hummed steady underneath it all.

moments.say: I set down the grass to catch the slip, while the card hums warm.

moments.say: The slip waits caught under the fence, heavy in the air.
